topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Waves

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Periodic Motion
lecture_lines: Periodic motion repeats its pattern indefinitely.
[Asset: Pendulum_Motion] Visualize this as a repeating wave.
Any periodic function f(x) equals f(x+T).
animations: Show cycle repetition with a circular path (#00FF00).

sections.title: The Core Intuition: The Harmonic Symphony
lecture_lines: Any complex wave is a sum of simple harmonics.
Think of this like stacking musical notes.
[Asset: Sine_Summation] Sine waves combine into a square wave.
Frequencies and amplitudes define our unique waveform.
The harmonic symphony reveals hidden structures.
animations: Draw a sine wave (#FFFFFF) representing a pure tone.
Overlay multiple sine waves to form a complex shape (#FFFF00).
Highlight the harmony between base frequencies (#00FFFF).

sections.title: The Mathematical Construction
lecture_lines: The Fourier series constructs complex periodic signals.
[Asset: Fourier_Formula] Each term acts as a weighted harmonic.
a₀ represents the signal's average height.
aₙ and bₙ are volume knobs for frequencies.
Adjusting coefficients reshapes the final function.
animations: Write the general summation formula using LaTeX (#FFFFFF).
Display the integration interval from 0 to T (#00FF00).
Connect the formula components with lines (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Calculation via Orthogonality
lecture_lines: We extract coefficients using the principle of orthogonality.
[Asset: Frequency_Filter] Signal passes through specific frequency gates.
The integral acts as a mathematical prism.

Demonstrate their inner product result of zero (#FF0000).

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
lecture_lines: Fourier series allow efficient signal processing.
[Asset: MP3_Compression] Removing frequencies shrinks file sizes.
We decompose signals to understand and reconstruct.
